title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
summary: We introduce several notions of resonance for systems exhibiting weak or partial dissipation: $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, with $A$ the generator of a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. We refer to resonance as the phenomenon where a time-periodic $f$ may yield an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, unbounded growth may depend on topological choices, and several ``resonances" may occur. Classically, existence of $T$-periodic $u$ under $T$-periodic $f$ is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$.…
